text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Singapore's largest industrial landlord, Jurong Town Corporation, will buy back more than 250 ha of land from its long-term tenants through an enbloc redevelopment programme which will cost more than S$1 billion.
- Eligible individuals can buy up to 1,000 NTUC FairPrice cooperative shares, up from the previous limit of 20 shares, while the ceiling of 5,000 shares for institutions has been lifted.

- Efforts to strengthen ties between Malaysia and Singapore must be doubled -- that was the consensus that emerged from meetings between a group of Singapore senior civil servants and Malaysian leaders yesterday.
- The Singapore dollar ended above S$1.50 to the US dollar, falling to a level not seen since September 1994.

- Singapore's better-than-expected economic growth of 7.8 percent in the second quarter was broad-based, with all sectors other than business services improving on their performances in the first three months of the year.
- The Philippines' Securities and Exchange Commission has ordered foreign consultancy firm Lee Goldman Asia Inc to shut down.
- The 80 percent housing loan limit is here to stay.

- Regional stock markets regained some poise following a firm Monday session in the US market, although the continued pressure on the ringgit and the Sing dollar capped any attempt at a meaningful rally.
- A 12 percent surge in electronics output in June helped propel the manufacturing sector into positive territory in that quarter, after three successive quarters of negative growth.
- Slackening demand for housing loans has taken its toll on Singapore's largest finance company, Hong Leong Finance, which reported flat half-year results.
- The selloff in the foreign shares of six large companies has wiped billions of dollars off the local bourse's market capitalisation in just a few days.

- Record company Form Holdings received in-principle approval for a Sesdaq listing. The initial public offering is expected to take place within a month at an offer price close to 40 cents sources said.
- Listed Omni Industries is beefing up its presence in China with a S$13.5 million investment on a big plant and machinery in Shanghai.
